newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mixed although roaster buying, gains in New York and worries over the threat of Mexican frost aided sentiment. January lost $8 to close at $1,307 per tonne, while March added $2 to close at $1,206 per tonne. The main unsettling factor, however, was a surprise announcement from the exchange on validity of coffee grading certificates following changes, announced in March, on the way robusta coffee is graded. LIFFE said grading certificates that have been issued and will continue to be issued against the current grading criteria will be valid for coffee tendered for delivery for January, March and May 1997 contracts only.

Coffee that is tendered for delivery against July 1997 and subsequent delivery months must have been graded against, and be accompanied by a valid grading certificate issued against the amended criteria. In New York arabica futures ended broadly higher with front month March adding 2.00 cents/lb to close at 111.90 cents/lb while May added 1.85 cents/lb to close at 109.00 cents/lb. The outer months closed 1.25 to 2.00 cents/lb higher. The rise was due to concerns about the possible damage to the Mexican coffee crop from expected low temperatures. However, the risk of damage is minimal, informed sources said. What has traders concerned is not loss to the actual beans of the 1996/97 harvest but possible reduction in quality of the crop. It could also affect next year's output.

KENYA - According to the Mild Coffee Traders Association coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) will reach not more than 1.42 million 60-kg bags, down from early estimates of 1.67 million bags, mainly because of an outbreak of coffee berry disease in the main growing areas around Mount Kenya. The lower forecast represents a decline in output of 11 percent from the 1.6 million bags produced in the 1995/96 season, it was added.

BRAZIL - The Brazilian government sold 86,284 60-kg bags of coffee or 95.85 percent of its auction on December 18 of 90,018 bags of stocks, official sources said. Prices ranged between 95.05 and 115.40 Reais ($91.40 and $110.96) a bag, it was added. The next auction is scheduled to be held on January 8.

IRELAND - Ireland imported 74,200 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 9 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 15 percent to 114,900 bags. Ireland gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from the United Kingdom.
